data.name: Peace
data.gender_notes: Peace is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Peace (Εἰρήνη, Eirene) was a goddess who personified peace, friendship, and concord. In the Bible, peace is a fruit of the Spirit and a promise from God. The name Peace carries the meaning “Absence of conflict” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Peace usually hope their child will grow to embody absence of conflict and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Peace belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Absence of conflict.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Peace total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, peace holds a profound and intimate spiritual significance, symbolizing harmony and wholeness with oneself, others, and with God. Peace is one of the fruits of the Holy Spirit mentioned in Galatians 5:22-23. It is also a promise in Isaiah 53:5, "But he was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed." This spiritual significance resonates with the words of Jesus in John 14:27, "Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled and do not be afraid."
